mechanism.summary: Answer an already-installed ordinary OwnSlot named-read cache entry on its hot path using a predecoded entry-kind hint and one transferred cache borrow, retaining identity, layout and live data-slot guards. Reuse the existing unpromoted implementation at 95c3af21 and supplement cache-state-transition and observable fallback tests.
mechanism.generality: The optimization depends only on cache entry kind, ordinary receiver identity and layout, and the current data slot. It applies to any named read that installs an OwnSlot entry; no workload identity, source text, function name, bytecode template, iteration count, value or checksum selects it. Exact, literal, shared and prototype entries keep their existing dispatch; accessors and exotic values keep ordinary fallback.
semantic_risks: A hint must remain synchronized across entry installation, selected-entry replacement, Exact-to-OwnSlot writes and clear, but must never substitute for live semantic guards.
Writes must observe the current value; deletion, insertion and descriptor-to-accessor changes must reject stale slots before inherited lookup or user code.
Cache borrows must end before getter or Proxy execution; weak receiver entries must not keep receivers or former values alive.
The new helper can perturb code generation and layout of unrelated hot paths; preserve the complete broad, external and sentinel regression gates and verify layout on the exact x86_64 binary.

profile_evidence.shared_cost: 64/528 main-thread samples pass through the ordinary named-property cold path get_prop_named; this includes necessary slot reads and is an envelope, not an estimate that all of it can be removed. Cold probe followed by own_data_slot_value independently confirms live OwnSlot reads. A guarded hot answer avoids repeated cold dispatch and probing without caching a value.
